Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:10:1.english: For me, it is worth [this] to me - I appraise it for myself, and I will accept it for that [amount].

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:11:1.english: For he is a great man - And he does not walk with an uncovered head.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:11:2.english: From Kovei - [This is] the name of a place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:12:1.hebrew: ונתן לה דינר - מיד מקודשת, דקיבלה ליה לשם קידושין וע"מ שישלים תנאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:12:1.english: And he gave her a dinar - She is betrothed immediately, for she accepted it for the purpose of betrothal and on the condition that he fulfill his stipulation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:14:1.hebrew: הרשות בידו - שאין הקידושין חלין עד שתקבל את כולו, ואת אמרת: מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:14:1.english: It is in his power - For the betrothal does not take effect until she receives all of it, whereas you said: "[She is] betrothed."

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:15:1.english: With this maneh - For her mind is on the whole of it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:16:1.english: A flawed dinar - [The Gemara] explains [this] later.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:17:1.hebrew: כיצד דאמר במנה זו - ונמצא חסר דינר, אינה מקודשת. והיינו דקאמר: רצה אחד לחזור, הרשות בידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:17:1.english: How so? Where he said: With this maneh - And [if] it was found lacking a dinar, she is not betrothed; and that is what it means when it says: If one [of them] wishes to retract, it is in their power [to do so].

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:18:1.english: It is reasonable - That [the latter clause] is explaining [the first clause].

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:18:2.english: Now, in [the case of] an unspecified *maneh* - [The Tanna] taught that they can retract as long as she has not received all of it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:18:3.hebrew: במנה זו - ונמצא חסר, דהשתא לא קבלה כולה, מיבעי' דמצי הדרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:18:3.english: With this maneh - And it was found deficient, since now she has not received all of it — is it necessary [to state] that she can retract?

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:20:1.hebrew: מונה והולך שאני - ואע"ג דאמר במנה סתם, כיון דחזיתיה מונה והולך, דעתה אכולה. אבל כי לא נתן לה אלא דינר וקבילתיה, ודאי לשם קידושין קבילתיה, ועל מנת שישלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:20:1.english: [A case where he] was counting is different - And even though he said "with a maneh" without specification, since she saw him counting [out the coins], her mind is on the entirety [of the sum]. However, when he gave her only a dinar and she accepted it, she certainly accepted it for the sake of betrothal, and on the condition that he will complete [the remainder].

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:21:1.hebrew: דאישתכח ביני זוזי - ולא הכירה בו מתחילה, שהיה מעורב ביניהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:21:1.english: That it was found among the coins - And she did not recognize it initially, as it was mixed in among them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:22:1.english: This is a copper dinar - And why is she betrothed?

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:2:1.english: Out of the money that he was bought for - It is written regarding a Hebrew slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:3:1.hebrew: ישיב גאולתו - ישיב קרא יתירא הוא, דמצי למכתב ״לפיהן גאולתו״, לרבות שוה כסף לענין פדיון. וכיון דמיפרוק ביה, איקנויי נמי מקנה ביה, דכתיב ״גאולתו מכסף מקנתו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:3:1.english: He shall return his redemption - “He shall return” is a superfluous word in the verse, as it could have written: “According to them [is] his redemption,” [and it comes] to include that which is worth money with regard to redemption. And since he may be redeemed with it, he may also be acquired with it, as it is written: “His redemption from the money of his purchase.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:4:1.hebrew: וכיון דלא קייץ לא - וה"ק: ואינו נקנה בתבואה וכלים, אלא א"כ קצץ דמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:4:1.english: And since [their value] is not set, no - And this is what [the baraita] is saying: And he is not acquired with grain and vessels unless he fixed their value.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:5:1.hebrew: בתורת כסף וכו' - בתורת דמים הוא נקנה: בין שנותנין עליו כסף, בין שוה כסף — בתורת דמים אקנו, ולא בתורת חליפין, שדרך לעשות חליפין בתבואה וכלים. כלים — שנאמר (רות ד׳:ז׳) שלף איש נעלו; ותבואה נמי — דכתיב (שם) כל דבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:5:1.english: Through the mode of money, etc. - He is acquired through the mode of monetary value: whether they give money for him or the equivalent of money, they effect acquisition through the mode of monetary value, and not through the mode of symbolic exchange, for it is customary to perform symbolic exchange with grain and vessels. Vessels — as it is stated (Ruth 4:7): "A man drew off his shoe"; and grain as well — as it is written (ibid.): "Anything."

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:6:1.hebrew: ולרב נחמן דאמר - בפרק הזהב: פירי לא עבדי חליפין — אם נתן תבואה בתורת חליפין, כמו סודר, לקנות בהן שדה או שום דבר בחליפין, לא קנו. והאי "כל דבר" מפרש ליה: דהכל נקנה במנעל. השתא, ליכא למימר תורת תבואה וכלים היינו חליפין — מאי איכא למימר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:6:1.english: And according to Rav Naḥman, who said - In [the chapter] HaZahav [Bava Metzia 47a, that] produce cannot effect symbolic exchange: If one gave grain in the manner of symbolic exchange, like a scarf, to acquire a field or anything with them through symbolic exchange, they do not effect acquisition; and that [phrase], "all things" [in Ruth 4:7: "to confirm all things, a man drew off his shoe"], he explains it [to mean] that everything is acquired with a shoe. Now, it cannot be said that the mode of grain and vessels is symbolic exchange; [hence,] what can be said?

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:6:2.hebrew: אלא לעולם - ואינו נקנה בתבואה וכלים דקאמר, בדלית בהו שוה פרוטה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:6:2.english: Rather, actually - And that which it says, “and he is not acquired with grain and vessels,” [is referring to a case] where they do not have the value of a peruta.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:7:1.english: Their benefit is close - They are readily available to derive benefit from them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:8:1.hebrew: לפדיון בני - לחמש סלעים של פדיון הבכור, דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז): ״ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה בערכך כסף חמשת שקלים״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:8:1.english: For the redemption of my son - [That is,] for the five sela of the redemption of the firstborn, as it is written (Numbers 18:15–16): “And those that are to be redeemed from a month old shall you redeem, according to your valuation, for the money of five shekels.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:8:2.english: He has said nothing - Even if he gave it to the priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:9:1.hebrew: כל כמיניה - כי אמר בחמש סלעים? בתמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:9:1.english: Is it in his power - When he says "for five sela"? [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:9:2.hebrew: דשוי - ואפי' הכי, קתני רישא: לא אמר כלום, הואיל ולא נישומו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 8a:9:2.english: That they are worth - And even so, the first clause teaches: 'He has said nothing,' since they were not appraised.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:10:1.hebrew: רב כהנא שקל סודרא בפדיון הבן - משמע הכא דרב כהנא היה כהן. ותימה: דבסוף אלו עוברין (פסחים דף מט.) משמע דלא היה כהן, דקאמר: "אי לאו דנסיבי כהנתא לא גלאי". וי"ל: דתרי רב כהנא הוו. אי נמי, י"ל: דבשביל אשתו היה לוקח, כדאשכחן בפרק הזרוע (חולין דף קלב.): רב כהנא אכל בשביל אשתו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:10:1.english: "Rav Kahana took a cloth for the redemption of the son" - It is implied here that Rav Kahana was a priest. And [this is] difficult, as at the end of [the chapter] Elu Overin (Pesachim 49a), it is implied that he was not a priest, as he said: "Had I not married a priest's daughter, I would not have been exiled!" And one can say that there were two [sages named] Rav Kahana. Alternatively, one can say that he took [the cloth] on behalf of his wife, as we find in the chapter [entitled] HaZero'a (Chullin 132a): "Rav Kahana ate on behalf of his wife."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:11:1.hebrew: אבל כולי עלמא לא - וא"ת: מאי טעמא דלא מהני? מי גרע ממתנה ע"מ להחזיר, דאמרינן לעיל (קידושין דף ו:) דשמה מתנה? וי"ל: דאין הכי נמי, דמיגרע גרע — דהתם איכא דבר חשוב דהוי מתנה, אע"פ שנתן ע"מ להחזיר; אבל הכא גבי פדיון, לא היה שוה אותו סודר חמש סלעים, ומתחילה כשנתן לו לא יצא ידי נתינה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:11:1.english: "But with regard to everyone else, no" - And if you say: What is the reason that it is not effective? Is it any worse than a gift on condition that it be returned, as we say earlier (Kiddushin 6b) that it is considered a [valid] gift? And one can say: Indeed, it is worse — for there, there is a substantial item that constitutes a gift, even though he gave it on condition that it be returned; but here, regarding redemption, that scarf was not worth five selaim, and from the outset when he gave it to him, he did not fulfill [his] obligation of giving.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:18:1.hebrew: השתא במנה סתם לא הוו קידושין במנה זו מיבעיא - וא"ת: דלמא הא קמ"ל, דבמנה זו, אע"ג דלא חזרה בה — לא הוי קידושין, כיון שנמצא חסר? ויש לומר: דמרישא שמעת מינה, כיון דבמנה סתם יכולה לחזור בה ולא אמרינן "ישלים", אלמא לא חלו הקידושין כלל עד שישלים — הכי נמי, כי אמר לה "במנה זו" ונמצא חסר, לא חלו הקידושין, ואף ההשלמה לא מהניא; שהרי לא סמכה דעתה להשלמתו, אלא למנה שמראה לה — והרי הוא חסר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:18:1.english: Now, in [the case of] an unspecified maneh it is not a betrothal, is "with this maneh" necessary? - And if you say: Perhaps this comes to teach us that [in the case of] "with this maneh," even though she did not retract, it is not a betrothal, since it was found lacking? And one can say: From the first clause you can infer this: Since in [the case of] an unspecified maneh she can retract, and we do not say "[let him] complete [it]" — evidently the betrothal did not take effect at all until he completes [it] — so too, when he said to her "with this maneh" and it was found lacking, the betrothal did not take effect, and even completion does not help; for her mind did not rely on his completing it, but rather on the maneh that he was showing her — and behold, it is lacking.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:1:1.hebrew: אף שוה כסף דקיץ - הא דאמרינן לקמן (קידושין דף יב.): "ההוא גברא דקדיש בזוודא דאורדי, יתיב רב שימי בר חייא וקא מעיין בה: אי אית בה שוה פרוטה — אין, אי לא — לא" — לכאורה דומה דלא כרב יוסף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:1:1.english: "So too, an item worth money [must be] set" - That which we say below (Kiddushin 12a): "A certain man betrothed [a woman] with a bundle of tow, [and] Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya sat and examined it: if it contains the value of a peruta, yes; if not, no" — seemingly appears not in accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Yosef.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:5:1.hebrew: ומאי ניהו חליפין - אין עבד עברי נקנה בחליפין, ולא קונה עצמו בחליפין — דמה שהוא קונה בכסף נפקא לן מהאי קרא דמכסף מקנתו לקמן (קידושין דף יד:) — אבל עבד כנעני נקנה בחליפין. כדתני בפ' השולח (גיטין (דף לט:) גבי שקל כומתא ושדא בה, אמר לה: "קני האי וקנה נפשך". ומשמע: משום דהויא ליה כליו של מקנה — לא עשה ולא כלום, אבל בכליו של קונה — קנתה; ומתורת חליפין משמע, ולא בתורת כסף. וכך פירש רבינו חננאל שם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:5:1.english: "And what is it? Symbolic exchange" - A Hebrew slave is not acquired through symbolic exchange, nor does he acquire himself through symbolic exchange, for that which he acquires [himself] with money is derived for us from this verse of "out of the money that he was bought for" below (Kiddushin 14b). However, a Canaanite slave is acquired through symbolic exchange, as it is taught in the chapter HaSholeiach (Gittin 39b) regarding [the incident where a master] took his hat and threw it to her, [and] said to her: "Acquire this and acquire yourself." And it implies that [only] because it was the utensil of the transferor (kelyo shel makneh) he accomplished nothing, but [had it been] with the utensil of the acquirer (kelyo shel koneh), she would have acquired [herself]; and it implies [that this acquisition was] through the mode of symbolic exchange, and not through the mode of money. And so explained Rabbeinu Ḥananel there.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 8a:8:1.english: "From where do I say [this]? As it is taught: 'This calf...'" - [Rav Yosef] brings a proof for the first version [of the dispute].
